The last series of actions show that I successfully rewrote the front‑end files (index.html, style.css, app.js), ran the test suite and lint, and then launched a preview server for the Studio UI. The server started on port 8426 and responded with HTTP 200 for the root page, the SVG logo, and the xterm.js vendor script, and the document’s readyState is "complete". However, attempts to capture a screenshot of the preview keep timing out, even after confirming there are no console errors. This suggests that the preview UI is either not rendering anything visible (perhaps the page is blank or stuck in a state that prevents the screenshot tool from grabbing the frame), or the screenshot tool itself is failing for some reason.

Given that the HTTP responses are fine, the static assets are being served correctly, and there are no console logs, the problem is likely within the page content itself. I need to investigate what the page actually contains when loaded. Since I cannot get a screenshot, I can probe the DOM via the preview_eval tool, but I already checked document.readyState and it is "complete". I could also query for the presence of key elements (e.g., the <svg> element with id or class, the <div id="app">, etc.) but the preview_eval tool only returns simple JavaScript evaluation results; it may be cumbersome to inspect the whole DOM that way.

Another angle: the page references the logo SVG at /static/teich.svg. I know from earlier that the SVG file is large (≈850 KB) and contains a lot of path data. Perhaps the SVG is malformed or contains data URIs that cause rendering issues in the preview environment. It would be useful to examine the SVG file directly to see its structure – count how many <path> elements it contains, and whether it includes any embedded raster data (e.g., an <image> tag with a data:image/png;base64 payload). If the SVG contains an embedded PNG, that could be problematic for the preview renderer, especially if the PNG data is large.

Therefore, I should inspect the SVG file located at src/teich/studio/static/teich.svg. A quick way is to run grep commands: count occurrences of the string "image/png;base64" to see if there is an embedded PNG, and count the number of <path> tags to gauge complexity. Additionally, I need to verify that the Python Imaging Library (PIL) is available in the environment, because later I might want to rasterize or manipulate the SVG. I can do a quick Python one‑liner that imports PIL and prints a confirmation.

All of these checks can be combined into a single Bash command: first grep for the base64 PNG marker, then count <path> tags, then run a Python snippet importing PIL. I’ll pipe the combined output through tail -1 to get the final line (the PIL availability check) after the two grep counts. This will give me a concise summary of the SVG composition and whether PIL is installed.

Thus, the appropriate next step is to execute a Bash tool call with that combined command.Assistant (tool call) Bash input={"command": "grep -o 'image/png;base64' src/teich/studio/static/teich.svg | wc -l; grep -c \"<path\" src/teich/studio/static/teich.svg; uv run python -c \"\nfrom PIL import Image\nprint('pil available')\n\" 2>&1 | tail -1", "description": "Inspect SVG composition and PIL availability"}

" 2>&1 | tail -1
